    EmailLinkLoginMethod
    WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration.emailLinkLoginMethod(WhoOneTimeTokenService tokenService, JsonGenerateOneTimeTokenRequestResolver generateRequestResolver, EmailLinkGenerationSuccessHandler generationSuccessHandler, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper> jsonMapper, JsonAuthenticationHandlers handlers, WhoService whoService, EmailLinkTokenRepository emailLinkTokenRepository, EmailLinkSettings settings, Clock clock, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher, WhoPaths paths)
    The provider and the converter are built here rather than published as beans: a lone AuthenticationProvider bean would become Spring Security's global one and switch off the application's UserDetailsService, and Spring's resource server takes any AuthenticationConverter bean as its own, so bearer requests would be read as sign-in codes.
